question: Which part of the skeleton includes the bones of the upper limbs?
explanation: The appendicular skeleton is made up of the bones of the upper and lower limbs, along with the shoulder and pelvic girdles. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h1)

question: What is the main advantage of how the upper limbs are designed?

options.C: Providing high mobility and hand control

explanation: Unlike the lower limbs which are built for stability and weight-bearing, the upper limbs are designed for a wide range of motion and precise hand movements. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h1)

question: What is the name of the shallow socket on the shoulder blade that forms the shoulder joint?
explanation: The glenoid cavity connects with the head of the upper arm bone to form the ball-and-socket shoulder joint. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h2)

question: Why is the collarbone important for the upper limb?

options.A: It holds the shoulder away from the chest for better movement.
options.B: It bears the full weight of the upper body during lifting.
options.C: It connects the arm bones directly to the spine.
options.D: It contains the main blood vessels for the hand.

explanation: The collarbone keeps the shoulder joint out to the side of the trunk, allowing the arm to swing freely without hitting the ribcage. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h2)

question: What is the single bone found in the upper arm?
explanation: The humerus is the only bone in the upper arm, extending from the shoulder down to the elbow. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why do clinicians pay close attention to fractures near the upper part of the arm bone?

options.A: It can easily damage the nearby axillary nerve.
options.B: It prevents any movement at the wrist joint.
options.C: It affects the main growth plate in adults.
options.D: It stops blood flow to the entire hand.

explanation: This area of the bone lies close to the pathway of the axillary nerve, making nerve injury a major risk when fractures happen here. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which forearm bone forms the bony point of the elbow when the arm is bent?
explanation: The top part of the ulna forms the prominent bony tip at the back of the elbow joint. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h4)

question: What movement happens when the forearm rotates to turn the palm downward?
explanation: Pronation is the forearm movement that turns the palm to face backward or downward. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h4)

question: How many small bones make up the wrist in one human hand?
explanation: There are eight small carpal bones arranged in two rows within the human wrist. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h5)

question: How do the finger bones of the thumb differ from the other fingers?

options.A: The thumb has no small finger bones at all.
options.B: The thumb contains only two finger bones instead of three.
options.C: The thumb bones are fused directly to the hand bones.
options.D: The thumb contains four small bones for gripping.

explanation: While the index through little fingers each have three sections, the thumb has only two sections. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h5)

question: What type of joint is primarily found at the elbow?
explanation: The elbow mainly acts as a hinge joint, allowing the arm to bend and straighten. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h6)

question: Why is the shoulder joint able to move in so many directions?

options.A: It lacks any fluid to reduce friction during movement.
options.B: It contains rigid bony blocks that prevent sideways movement.
options.C: It has a very deep socket that tightly locks the bone in place.
options.D: It features a shallow socket paired with a large arm bone head.

explanation: The shallow nature of the shoulder socket allows the large head of the arm bone to glide freely through a wide range of motion. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of a standard check for blood flow and nerve function in an injured arm?

options.C: Checking pulse strength at the wrist
options.D: Checking capillary refill time in the fingers

explanation: These specific checks focus on circulation, feeling, and movement in the affected limb, rather than general body temperature. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h7)

question: A patient falls on an outstretched hand and hurts their wrist. What primary complication must be monitored closely?

options.D: Compromised blood flow and nerve damage

explanation: Swelling and shifting bones near blood vessels and nerves at the wrist can quickly cut off circulation or feeling to the hand. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T11#BMP111_U2_T11_h7)
